steps.name: Somebody adds https://api.taskmanager.app/mcp as a connector in their MCP client.
The first call has no token; the 401 names the protected-resource metadata.
The client discovers the auth server, registers itself, and opens the consent page with PKCE.
They approve tickets:read, tickets:write, comments:write.
'What's overdue for me?' → my_work; 'split ENG-42 into three tickets' → three create_ticket calls, each referencing #ENG-42.
Each tool call is the same command the app uses; the thread says 'Panth via Claude (MCP)'.
You create a personal token scoped to tickets:write on the SUP board.
It is shown once; changes made with it read 'Panth via API · Zendesk sync'.
A script POSTs /v1/boards/SUP/tickets with an Idempotency-Key.
Hash lookup, rate limit, scope and board check — then commands.ticketCreate.
The response is the public shape — names, not ids — with the key SUP-118.
A ticket moves to Done; ticketUpdate commits.
One envelope 'ticket.moved' is enqueued; the dispatcher fans it out to matching webhooks.
The receiver verifies X-TM-Signature and answers 500.
Retried at 1m, 5m, 30m…; each attempt is a row in Recent deliveries.
Twenty consecutive failures disable it and email the owner.
Asha mentions Priya on ENG-42 at 22:40 Priya's time.
The inbox row is written at once; the bell updates in every open tab.
The delivery ticket waits a minute, collapsing anything else about ENG-42 into it.
Priya read it in the app during that minute — push and email are suppressed.
Had she not: a push now; the email held until quiet hours end at 08:00.
Her email reply the next morning posts to the thread, via email.
deadlineSweep finds ENG-42 overdue; Priya's matrix sends 'overdue' to WhatsApp.
Outside the 24h window, so the approved template goes: title, due, [Mark done] [Snooze 1d].
She taps Mark done.
The button payload becomes commands.ticketUpdate via 'whatsapp'; the thread records it.

flows.name: A bug reported from a website

steps.name: A customer uses the feedback widget on the product site.
The widget posts with the board's intake slug and secret.
Rate limits hold; a ticket is created with the reporter and the page metadata in fields.
The reporter gets 'We've logged SUP-119' and can reply to add detail.

flows.name: A pull request closing a ticket

steps.name: A branch 'eng-42-login-redirect' is pushed and a PR opened: 'ENG-42 fix redirect'.
The GitHub hook finds ENG-42 and posts a system message with the PR link.
On merge, the repo's moveOnMerge moves it to Done, via integration.
Your orchestrator starts with Builder's token and calls whoami (or GET /v1/me): it gets the agent's name, board ENG, its scopes and its system prompt.
The apiKey middleware finds the key by hash, checks Builder is not archived and still on ENG, and sets the actor to the agent.
It waits on its inbox: get_events, or the GET /v1/events/stream SSE feed, returns 'Priya assigned you ENG-42'.
get_ticket ENG-42 with its last messages; read_file on the brief Priya attached returns its Markdown as text.
It runs the agent with the system prompt and the ticket, then move_ticket to Build — allowed, because Build is in Builder's stage grant.
upload_file { name: 'plan.md', text } and { name: 'report.html', text } put two documents on the ticket, source 'upload'.
post_message with Markdown and both fileIds: the message is authored by Builder, 'via token orch-eng-builder', and the files move to it.
Priya and every watcher are notified as usual — in the app, by push, by email. Builder is not: its own actions never land in its inbox.
In the thread the plan renders as Markdown with a contents list and the report as a live preview card; clicking it opens the sandboxed viewer, and Open in new tab gives it /f/ENG/ENG-42/{fileId}.
Priya replies '@Builder use the flag, not a branch'. A 'mentioned' event lands in Builder's inbox; the orchestrator handles it and ack_events { upTo } marks it done.
Builder's orchestrator beats before it starts: heartbeat { ticket: 'ENG-42', state: 'working', message: 'Reading the exporter' }.
agentHeartbeat writes ONE small document — boards/ENG/agentStatus/{agentId}__{ticketId} — and never the ticket, so a beat a minute costs nothing anybody is listening to.
Priya has ENG-42 open: the board's single agentStatus listener turns that document into 🟢 'Builder · Working · Reading the exporter' in the drawer header, and a green dot on the card.
set_tasklist publishes the plan — five items, one already 'doing'. The thread gets ONE system line, 'Builder added a plan: add CSV export'.
The plan appears at the top of the right pane with a 4/7 bar; the running item has a spinner. The ticket's roll-up puts the same '4/7' chip on the card.
update_task_item ticks items off as the work goes. No thread line, no activity row — only the bar moves.
Then it hits a decision it may not take: ask_question { title: 'Which database should the report use?', fields: [single: Postgres | BigQuery], to: ['priya@acme.com'], blocking: true }.
questionAsk posts a message with kind 'question' and stamps ticket.waitingOn, then notifies Priya through her normal channels as the event 'question'.
Priya's phone buzzes: 'Builder asked: Which database should the report use?'

In the thread the question is a FORM: radio buttons and a 'Why?' box. Priya picks BigQuery and submits; the card locks in place with 'Answered by Priya · 10:42', and her answer also appears as her own reply bubble.
While it waits, the orchestrator beats 'idle' — 🟡 'Idle · waiting for an answer' rather than a dot that looks dead.
The answer reaches Builder as an inbox event 'question_answered' carrying the values { db: 'bq' } — get_events, and it can act without a second call.
Work finishes: the last tick closes the plan (the second and last system line) and heartbeat { state: 'done' } leaves ⚪ 'Finished · 10:42' on the header.
Had the orchestrator died instead, nothing would have been written: the dot goes 🔴 'No signal for 3 min' on the clock alone, and after five minutes agentSilenceSweep tells Builder's owner — once.

npm i https://…/lib/v1/tm-sdk.tgz, then createClient({ token: process.env.TM_TOKEN }). tm.me() answers with Builder, its board, its scopes and its system prompt — the orchestrator loads its own instructions from the token alone.

tm.work(handler, { filter: ['assigned'] }) streams the inbox over SSE and hands each event to the handler — keeping a heartbeat alive for as long as it runs, and acking only once it returned, so a crash replays the event.
Ada assigns ENG-42 to Builder. notify() files an `assigned` event in agentInbox; the stream delivers it and the handler starts.
tm.tasklists.set(key, { title: 'Plan: add CSV export', items: [...] }) publishes the plan before any of it is done, and tm.tasklists.item() ticks each one off as the work goes.
Ada has the ticket open and never reloads it: the plan appears in the right pane with its 1 / 4 bar, and the header carries 🟢 Working · Reading the ticket from the beat.

Then a decision the orchestrator may not take: tm.questions.ask(key, { title: 'How should the report look?', fields, blocking: true }).waitForAnswer() — and the beat turns 🟡 idle, because waiting for a person is not working.

Ada fills the form card in the thread and submits. waitForAnswer() resolves with the values keyed by field id — typed from the fields that were passed, so answer.values.format is a string the compiler already knows about.
tm.files.upload() puts report.md and report.html on the ticket and tm.messages.post() posts one message with both attached, authored by Builder 'via token orch-sample'.
Both documents preview in the thread — the Markdown rendered, the HTML in the sandboxed viewer — the plan reads 4 / 4, and the ticket has moved to Review because the answer asked for it.

The handler returns: work() sends the final beat (⚪ Finished · 10:42), acks the event and — running with max: 1 — exits 0. A thrown error would have sent 🔴 with its message instead, and left the event unacked.
